body:
I really love mini.files — it’s incredibly fast for navigating directory structures and offers the same intuitive editing style that I enjoy from oil.nvim.

There’s one area, though, where I often run into friction: editing file or directory names that require horizontal movement. When I’m trying to move the cursor left or right during a rename, I occasionally press h or l in normal mode out of habit. Since those keys are bound to navigation/open actions in mini.files, this can cause accidental directory jumps or opening files unintentionally.

Doing simple operations like delete or move feels very smooth, but more precise text-editing inside a filename sometimes becomes tricky because of these conflicting key behaviors.

Feature Proposal: “Edit Mode” Toggle

I think it would be extremely useful to have a keybinding that:
	•	Locks mini.files into a dedicated “edit mode”, where its normal navigation mappings (like h/l) are temporarily disabled,
	•	Allows the user to freely use full normal-mode text editing keys to adjust file/dir names,
	•	And then, with another toggle, exit edit mode and return to regular mini.files navigation behavior.

This would let users make precise edits without worrying about triggering unintended file-navigation actions.

I haven’t used [oil.nvim](https://github.com/stevearc/oil.nvim), so I can’t say how good it is, but sometimes it’s just not worth overcomplicating things. Still, I might be wrong here.

> What I am suggesting is a way to turn on an "oil" mode so you can get a pure editing experience without have to rethink anything.

Unfortunately, you would still have to "rethink" *something* based on [how manipulation tracking works](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-files.html#minifiles-manipulation-howdoesitwork). I believe 'oil.nvim' has similar behavior.

And, of course, having both 'mini.files' and 'oil.nvim' installed feels like an overfitting to one particular case. I don't think the issue brought up here is bad enough to resort to other plugin for manipulating file system.

I can't speak to the complexity of implementing this. In my mind which could be way off, the implementation would be a simple key map that toggles (enables/disables) the mini.files navigation based keymaps; not navigation within the buffer but across directory buffers. So it's not truly a "new mode" it's just a way to temporarily disable directory movement so you get full access to normal mode editing.

If this somehow breaks the way mini.files tracks changes then I can see why this would be a no-go. Hopefully I am explaining this clearly. No worries if you still think this isn't a possible feature. Fyler seems to have solved this but it lacks the quick navigation across directories that I think makes mini.files stand out amongst all other file tree solutions.

reply_data.body:
For what it's worth (in case anyone else is looking for this sort of thing), the implementation was pretty easy and works for what I was hoping for. If inside a mini.files buffer, \<Leader\>ee essentially disables the navigation behavior (go_in/go_out) so I can edit with full normal mode; pressing again resumes normal navigation behavior. Obviously the below can be more robust since this assume users are using h, l for moving across directories but in my set up this works fine and does exactly what I would have expected it to.

```lua
		-- Custom Edit Mode Toggle for mini.files
		local edit_mode_active = false
		local function toggle_edit_mode()
		    edit_mode_active = not edit_mode_active
		    if edit_mode_active then
			vim.keymap.del('n', 'h', { buffer = buf_id })
			vim.keymap.del('n', 'l', { buffer = buf_id })
			vim.notify('MiniFiles: Edit mode enabled', vim.log.levels.INFO)
		    else
			vim.keymap.set('n', 'h', function() minifiles.go_out() end, { buffer = buf_id, desc = 'Minifiles: Left navigation' })
			vim.keymap.set('n', 'l', function() minifiles.go_in() end, { buffer = buf_id, desc = 'Minifiles: Right navigation' })
			vim.notify('MiniFiles: Edit mode disabled', vim.log.levels.INFO)
		    end
		end
		-- Toggle edit mode with <Leader>ee
		vim.keymap.set('n', '<Leader>ee', toggle_edit_mode, { buffer = buf_id, desc = 'Toggle MiniFiles Edit Mode' })
```

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the idea!

This sounds interesting (and not a bad idea per se, @drowning-cat). I've definitely been burnt by this use case in the past.

However, my suggestion is to use different forms of horizontal navigation instead of `j` and `k` when inside explorer window. I usually resort to `fFtT` keys. For example, `fa` to navigate to the letter which is start of the change and `ct.` to change file/directory name's suffix (but keep extension).

There are also other ways of mitigating this:
- Use arrows.
- Enter Insert mode and navigate within it. Like with 'mini.basics' `<M-hjkl>`.
- Remap `go_in` and `go_out` keys as [@drowning-cat suggested](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2149#discussioncomment-15122500).

So all in all, I think adding this type of complexity to 'mini.files' doesn't fit the whole 'mini.nvim' design, since there are solid workarounds.
